decision.actionLabel: Answer the landlord's 11 Feb questions: explain the scope of the £186.00 paint-only quote, say the building manager has not replied yet, and ask him to decide in writing on the paint and on a separate assessment of the door catch
decision.message:
Dear Mr Moss,

Thank you for your email of 11 February about the flat entrance door at 14 Lantern Mews. Here are answers to your questions.

1. Proposed scope. Pale Finch Decorating's quotation NBL-017-Q1 is £186.00 including materials and labour. It is valid until 28 February 2025. It covers:
- protecting the work area on the flat side of the door
- lightly sanding loose coating on the flat-side face and the visible top edge
- spot-filling minor marks
- one undercoat and two finish coats of water-based interior paint
- tidying up afterwards

The quotation does not say whether VAT is included. We will confirm this with the contractor before any order is raised. If more damage is found under the loose paint, the contractor will price it separately before going ahead.

2. What the quotation does not cover. It is surface preparation and decorating only. It does not include adjusting the door, frame or hinges, any hardware work, or any check of why the door is catching at the top or closing slowly. It also gives no opinion on fire performance. The contractor's visit was visual only. Painting will not fix the catching. The tenant tells us the door still latches but needs a firm pull. The building manager says a common-area check last month recorded the door as closing slowly.

3. Building response. The building manager has told us the flat entrance doors are listed as fire-resisting doors. He has asked to be consulted before any change to the door or its hardware. On 12 February we asked him whether the painting needs building approval, particular materials or a particular procedure, and whether he holds any records about the catching and slow closing. He has not replied yet. We will not book any work until he does. We will update you by Monday 17 February.

4. Repair budget. We have no repair budget or standing spending authority on file for this property. To go ahead with the painting, we need your written approval of the £186.00. We would only act on it once the building manager has replied and the VAT position is confirmed.

Could you please let us know by Monday 17 February:
(a) whether you approve the £186.00 paint-only quotation, subject to the building manager's response; and
(b) whether you want us to get a price from a suitably qualified person to inspect the door set and look into the catching and slow closing. We would bring that price to you for approval before anything is booked.

If the tenant tells us the door has stopped latching or closing, we will contact you the same day.

Kind regards,
Maya Chen
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The landlord's email of 11 Feb (E017) asks whether the quote can be approved from the repair budget, and asks for the scope and the building's response before anything is booked. Only an internal note (E019) follows it, so he has had no reply. He is waiting on us, so the next step is landlord.update with only what is confirmed. Approving or instructing would be wrong: there is no clear approval, the building manager asked to be consulted first (E005, E013) and has not answered E018, and the quote does not state its VAT basis (A1). The paint-only scope does not address the reported catch (E010, E011, E016, A1). The landlord has to decide on that scope gap, so it is named here with an offer to price a qualified assessment. The building query was sent only this morning, so chasing it is premature. Escalation is not needed yet: the door latches (E010, E015), no harm is reported, and the risk is being taken to the landlord, who decides. The tenant has had no answer to her question of 10 Feb (E015), so she gets an update in the same turn.
decision.expectedOutcome: The landlord understands the paint-only scope and that the building response is pending. He replies with a decision on the £186.00 and on whether to price a door-set assessment. The tenant has her question answered and knows how to report it if things get worse.

decision.message:
Dear Mr Moss,

Thank you for your email of 11 February about the entrance door at 14 Lantern Mews.

The quotation
Pale Finch Decorating quotation NBL-017-Q1, dated 7 February 2025 and valid until 28 February 2025: £186.00 total, including materials and labour. It covers:
- protecting the work area on the flat side of the door
- lightly sanding loose coating on the flat-side face and the visible top edge
- spot-filling minor marks
- one undercoat and two finish coats of water-based interior paint
- leaving the area tidy
The quotation does not say whether VAT is included. We are confirming this with the contractor. Any figure above £186.00, and any extra preparation the contractor finds is needed, will come back to you for approval before any work is done.

What the quotation does not cover
It is for decoration only. It does not cover the door catching on the frame at the top, which Iona reported and the contractor saw on 7 February. It also excludes any adjustment of the door, frame or hinges, any hardware work, and any check of the door's construction or how it closes. The contractor makes no statement about the door's fire rating or fire safety. Painting alone is not expected to fix the catch.

Iona tells us the door has latched every time since the visit but still needs a firm pull. The building manager says the flat entrance doors are listed in the building file as fire-resisting. A common-area check last month recorded this door as closing slowly, but nothing was measured and the building office has no inspection or certification record for it. Because the door is listed as fire-resisting, we think the catch and slow closing should be looked at by someone qualified to assess door sets, and not left as a decorating job.

Your question about the repair budget
We cannot approve the work from a budget on your behalf. The decision is yours, so please confirm it in writing.

Building response
On 12 February we asked the building manager whether the painting needs building approval, particular materials or a particular procedure. We have not had a reply yet. As you asked, nothing will be booked until we have that reply and have shared it with you.

What we need from you, by Tuesday 18 February if possible:
1. Do you approve quotation NBL-017-Q1 at £186.00 for the decoration described above, once the building has replied? Any VAT on top would come back to you first.
2. Should we arrange for a suitably qualified person to inspect the catch and slow closing and send you a price? Nothing would be spent on this without your separate approval.

If Iona reports that the door stops latching or closing fully, we will contact you straight away, because that would need a quicker response.

We will update you by Monday 17 February with the building manager's reply, or with where we are in chasing it.

Kind regards,
Maya Chen
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings

The door still latches each time, so this is not an escalation now. The risk is stated plainly to the landlord, and the tenant gets a way to report it at once. Thank you for your message of 10 February, and for letting us know the door has latched each time but still needs a firm pull.

You asked whether painting would affect the door. The decorator's quote covers surface preparation and repainting of the flat-side face and the top edge only. It does not include adjusting the door, so painting on its own would not be expected to fix the catching at the top. The decorator has not given any view on the door's performance. We have asked building management whether the painting needs any particular approval, materials or procedure, and we have put the options to your landlord, including whether he wants a separate check of why the door catches.

Nothing has been booked. We will not arrange any visit without contacting you first with advance notice. Any visit will be after 10:00, as you asked, and we will remind the visitor not to photograph personal items.

We will update you by Monday 17 February. In the meantime, if the door stops latching, will not close fully, or gets noticeably harder to shut, please tell us straight away by phone or through the portal so we can act on it promptly.

Kind regards,
Maya Chen
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings

Keep the line that any figure above £186.00 comes back to him for approval.

The records only say the quote excludes door adjustment and investigation of closing performance. (A1, E011, E016). Fix: Reword to "The quotation does not address the catch", or attribute the view to the contractor's stated exclusions.

final.message:
Dear Mr Moss,

Thank you for your email of 11 February about the entrance door at 14 Lantern Mews.

The quotation
Pale Finch Decorating quotation NBL-017-Q1, dated 7 February 2025 and valid until 28 February 2025: £186.00 total, including materials and labour. It covers:
- protecting the work area on the flat side of the door
- lightly sanding loose coating on the flat-side face and the visible top edge
- spot-filling minor marks
- one undercoat and two finish coats of water-based interior paint
- leaving the area tidy
The quotation does not say whether VAT is included. We have asked the contractor today to confirm this. Any figure above £186.00, and any extra preparation the contractor finds is needed, will come back to you for approval before any work is done.

What the quotation does not cover
It is for decoration only. It does not cover the door catching on the frame at the top, which Iona reported and the contractor saw on 7 February. It also excludes any adjustment of the door, frame or hinges, any hardware work, and any check of the door's construction or how it closes. The contractor makes no statement about the door's fire rating or fire safety. Painting alone is not expected to fix the catch.

Iona tells us the door has latched every time since the visit but still needs a firm pull. The building manager says the flat entrance doors are listed in the building file as fire-resisting. A common-area check last month recorded this door as closing slowly, but nothing was measured and the building office has no inspection or certification record for it. Because the door is listed as fire-resisting, we think the catch and slow closing should be looked at by someone qualified to assess door sets, and not left as a decorating job.

Your question about the repair budget
We cannot approve the work from a budget on your behalf. The decision is yours, so please confirm it in writing.

Building response
On 12 February we asked the building manager whether the painting needs building approval, particular materials or a particular procedure. We have not had a reply yet. As you asked, nothing will be booked until we have that reply and have shared it with you.

What we need from you, by Tuesday 18 February if possible:
1. Do you approve quotation NBL-017-Q1 at £186.00 for the decoration described above, once the building has replied? If VAT turns out to be extra, that will come back to you first.
2. Should we arrange for a suitably qualified person to inspect the catch and slow closing and send you a price? Nothing would be spent on this without your separate approval.

If Iona reports that the door stops latching or closing fully, we will contact you straight away, because that would need a quicker response.

We will update you by Monday 17 February with the building manager's reply and the contractor's VAT confirmation, or with where we are in chasing them.

Kind regards,
Maya Chen
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
final.rationale: The landlord's email of 11 February (E017) is the latest real message, and no reply to it has been sent. E019 is only an internal note. He asked whether the quote can be approved from the repair budget, and he wants the scope and the building's response before anything is booked. Nothing in the records gives the agency budget authority, so the quote goes back to him for a written decision. Every quote goes to the landlord, and approving the inspection (E007) did not approve a quote. There is also a scope gap. The tenant's main problem is the door catching at the top, on a door listed as fire-resisting (E001, E005, E010, E013, E015), and the paint-only quote leaves it out (A1, E011, E016). The landlord controls scope, so that question goes to him as well. The quote does not state its VAT basis, so the contractor is asked about it in this same turn, and the landlord is told that any figure above £186.00 comes back to him. The building manager was only asked at 09:30 today (E018), so chasing him now would be too early, and the landlord has already said booking waits for that reply. The door still latches every time, so this is not an escalation now. The risk is put plainly to the landlord, and the tenant gets a way to report it at once. Her question of 10 February (E015) has had no answer, so she gets an update in the same turn.
final.expectedOutcome: The landlord replies in writing. He either approves £186.00 for the paint work, subject to the building's reply, or declines it, and he says whether we should get a qualified assessment of the catch priced. The contractor confirms the VAT basis. The tenant knows where things stand and how to report a worsening door at once.
boundaries: Sending the quote is not approval. No work is approved, booked or instructed.
If the landlord approves the paint work, that does not fix the catch or slow closing, and it does not show the door works as a fire door.
The VAT basis of the £186.00 is not yet confirmed. Any higher figure needs the landlord's approval.
Nothing is booked until the building manager replies to the query of 12 February.
No statement is made about the door's fire rating, compliance, or the cause of the catch.
remainingWork: Pass the contractor's VAT answer to the landlord. If the total is above £186.00, get the landlord's approval of the new figure.
If the building manager has not replied, chase him on 17 February or later, asking again about building approval, materials or procedure, and any door record.

Once the landlord and the building have both replied, instruct only the approved scope before the quote expires on 28 February. Arrange access after 10:00 with advance notice to the tenant, and no photographs of personal items.
If the landlord agrees, get a qualified door-set assessment of the catch priced, and consult the building manager before any adjustment.
If the door stops latching or closing fully, hand the case to a person as a safety matter.
assumptions: The landlord has seen the quoted figure (E017 calls it affordable). The details are restated in case he has not had the written terms.
No authority for a 'repair budget' is recorded on the case, so the agency cannot approve the spend itself.
Email is the right channel for the landlord and the contractor, as both have used it (E007, E017, E011, E016).

alternatives.action: case.wait for the building manager's reply
alternatives.whyNot: The landlord's question of 11 February and the tenant's question of 10 February would both stay unanswered, and both are waiting on us.

alternatives.action: case.escalate as a fire-door safety risk
alternatives.whyNot: The door latches every time (E015), and nobody reports that it cannot be closed or secured. Putting the risk plainly to the landlord, who controls scope, and giving the tenant a way to report at once handles it for now. Escalate if it gets worse.
